entries.title: A locked door, EA games, emulators, and a way to reach me
entries.summary: Sign-in now talks to the real Apex account server and cannot be pointed anywhere else, your EA App games are finally detected, there is a whole Emulators view, the Store stopped stuttering while you type, and there is a Contact page.

sections.title: New
items: An Emulators view. Apex finds the emulators you already have installed, walks your ROM folders, sorts what it finds onto a shelf per console and launches a title straight into the right emulator.
A panel of genuinely free ROM sources - archive.org public-domain sets, itch.io freeware, homebrew hubs, ScummVM and OpenTTD - so the shelf only ever points at things that are free to get.
Contact page: my Discord and Telegram, one click to copy or open.
A live clock in the top right corner.
EA App, Ubisoft Connect and Battle.net titles now carry their own store badge.
A small build stamp in the corner of the window, so you always know exactly which build you are running.

sections.title: Fixed
items: EA App and Origin games are detected properly. The old probe only read registry keys the modern EA App never writes, so those titles were invisible to Apex.
Game names from the registry keep their real characters. The trademark sign in a title was being silently rewritten to a letter T.

sections.title: Improved
items: The Store no longer rebuilds every card on every keystroke, which is where the stutter while searching came from.
The controller on-screen keyboard and the live search keep working exactly as before; only the wasted work is gone.

sections.title: Changed
items: The account server is compiled into the build. The sign-in screen has no server field and Settings shows the address read-only, so nobody can point the launcher at a different backend.

entries.title: Overlay, achievements and a proper goodbye
entries.summary: Performance overlay on F8, screenshots on F2, achievements you can actually earn, and an uninstall that deletes the files instead of hiding them.

sections.title: New
items: Uninstall or remove: deleting a game now really deletes it, and says exactly which folders and how much space first.
Performance overlay: F8 floats a click-through panel over any game with real CPU, GPU and RAM readings.
Screenshots: F2 grabs the screen, saves a PNG and files it in a gallery you can browse and prune.
Achievements: Apex awards its own from what you actually do, with a Steam-style toast, and can pull your real Steam achievements with your own Web API key.
What's new: a changelog bundled with the app, shown once each time it updates.

sections.title: Improved
items: The controller on-screen keyboard opens for every search box and has a button of its own.
Archive extraction reports a live percentage, so a long unrar no longer looks frozen.

sections.title: Notes
items: The overlay measures what it can honestly measure. A true in-game frame rate needs a graphics hook, so the panel labels its frame timing as the desktop's present rate and never claims to be the game's own.

entries.title: Nexus and the download engine
entries.summary: A new catalogue alongside a real multi-provider download pipeline.

sections.title: New
items: Nexus: search a second catalogue, with mirrors resolved per provider and automatic failover.
Tools: the Bypass, OnlineFix and SteamLess panels, with their catalogues refreshed from GitHub.
Downloads that start from the launcher with no window, no tab and no site to click through.
